name: COSMIN Reporting Guideline 2.0 (measurement properties of PROMs)
citation: Gagnier JJ, de Arruda GT, Terwee CB, Mokkink LB, et al. COSMIN reporting guideline for studies on measurement properties of patient-reported outcome measures: version 2.0. Qual Life Res 2025;34:1901-11. Supersedes version 1.0 (Gagnier JJ, Lai J, Mokkink LB, Terwee CB. Qual Life Res 2021;30:2197-218, doi:10.1007/s11136-021-02822-4). Items are numbered 1-68 here; each topic starts with the guideline's own identifier (T1 ... O1 general, CV1 ... Resp4 property-specific). See https://www.cosmin.nl

items.topic: T1 Title names a measurement-property study
items.question: Does the title make clear that the report studies measurement properties of a named PROM, for a stated construct and population?
Does the abstract state the aims, naming the PROM (and version), its construct, the properties assessed and key study features?
Does the abstract describe the design used to assess the measurement properties?
Does the abstract say how each measurement property was assessed?

items.topic: A4 Main results for every property
items.question: Does the abstract give the main result for every measurement property assessed?
Does the abstract close with what the findings mean, set against existing evidence on the PROM?

items.topic: I1 PROM name, version and construct
items.question: Does the introduction name the PROM, its version where relevant, and the construct(s) it measures?

items.topic: I2 Intended population and context of use
items.question: Is the population and the context of use the PROM was built for stated?
Is what is known and unknown about the PROM's measurement properties summarised, the need for this study argued, and its development paper(s) cited?
Are the objectives stated, naming the PROM (and version), the properties assessed and the relevant sample characteristics?
Is the design used to evaluate the measurement properties described in enough detail?
Is it explained how participants were selected, with inclusion and exclusion criteria?
Are the PROM's versions, model (reflective or formative), structure, language, response scale, recall period, scoring and administration described?

items.topic: GM4 Other data collected and why
items.question: Are other data collected (e.g. comparator instruments, group characteristics) described with their rationale and mode of administration?
Are all measurement time points given?
Is the sample size justified for every measurement-property analysis, subgroups included?

items.topic: GM7 Statistical methods and quality criteria
items.question: Are analyses described for every objective, with the criteria for good measurement properties and the software and version used?
Is it described how missing data were handled?
Are analyses that were not planned identified, with the reason for each?
Are participant characteristics reported, per subgroup where applicable?

items.topic: GR2 Sample size overall and per analysis
items.question: Are the total number of participants and the number in each analysis reported?

items.topic: GR3 Extent of and reasons for missing data
items.question: Are the amount of and reasons for missing data reported per analysis, for the PROM and for any other instrument?
Are results reported for every objective (see the property-specific items)?

items.topic: DC1 Main findings and sufficiency per property
items.question: Does the discussion give the main findings and judge each property sufficient or insufficient, with reasons?
Is the practical relevance discussed as advice on whether or not to use the PROM?
Are strengths and limitations discussed, including possible biases that could have affected the results?
Is it discussed whether the results generalise beyond the sample studied, e.g. to other populations?

items.topic: DC5 Needed changes to the PROM
items.question: Is it discussed what modifications, if any, the PROM needs?
Are the new questions or hypotheses the findings raise described, with the research needed to answer them?

items.topic: DC7 Overall conclusion on using the PROM
items.question: Is an overall conclusion given about the use of the PROM?

items.topic: O1 Conflicts of interest regarding the PROM
items.question: Are conflicts of interest related to the PROM declared, such as a role in developing it or commercial interests?
If the study evaluates content validity, is it described whether and how patients or professionals judged the relevance of instructions, items, response options and recall period?
If the study evaluates content validity, is it described whether and how patients or professionals judged that no key concept is missing?
If the study evaluates content validity, is it described whether and how patients or professionals judged how understandable the PROM's parts are?
If the study evaluates content validity, is it reported whether the PROM's parts were judged relevant to the construct, population and context of use?
If the study evaluates content validity, is it reported whether patients or professionals judged all key concepts to be covered?
If the study evaluates content validity, is it reported whether patients understood the PROM as intended, or professionals judged its wording appropriate?

items.topic: SV1 Rationale for the analytic approach
items.question: If the study evaluates structural validity, is the choice of approach (factor analysis, IRT/Rasch or other) justified?
If the study evaluates structural validity, are the tested model, estimation method and fit criteria (or the IRT/Rasch model, assumption checks and software) described?
If the study evaluates structural validity, are loadings and fit indices (or IRT/Rasch item parameters and fit) reported for the original and best-fitting models?
If the study evaluates internal consistency, are unidimensionality and lack of local dependence supported, and the statistic used described?
If the study evaluates internal consistency, are results given separately for each unidimensional scale or subscale?
If the study evaluates measurement invariance (cross-cultural validity), is the variable that defines the compared groups described?

items.topic: CCV2 Rationale for the analytic approach
items.question: If the study evaluates measurement invariance (cross-cultural validity), is the choice of approach (multi-group CFA, DIF analysis or other) justified?
If the study evaluates measurement invariance (cross-cultural validity), are the tested models, estimation and the criteria for flagging non-invariant or DIF items described?

items.topic: CCV4 Fit differences between tested models
items.question: If the study evaluates measurement invariance (cross-cultural validity), are the changes or differences in fit between the tested models reported?

items.topic: R1 Arguments that patients were stable
items.question: If the study evaluates reliability, is it argued why patients can be assumed stable on the construct between repeated measurements?

items.topic: R2 ICC or kappa form and justification
items.question: If the study evaluates reliability, is the specific ICC or kappa formula named and its choice justified?
If the study evaluates reliability, is it stated which source of variation (e.g. occasion, rater) was deliberately varied between measurements?

items.topic: R4 Appropriateness of the time interval
items.question: If the study evaluates reliability, is the interval between measurements argued to be appropriate?
If the study evaluates reliability, is it reported whether patients were in fact stable between measurements?
If the study evaluates reliability, are ICC or kappa values reported with standard errors or confidence intervals, and variance components or contingency tables?

items.topic: ME1 Arguments that patients were stable
items.question: If the study evaluates measurement error, is it argued why patients can be assumed stable on the construct between repeated measurements?

items.topic: ME2 SEM, SDC or LoA formula and rationale
items.question: If the study evaluates measurement error, is the formula for the SEM, smallest detectable change, limits of agreement or agreement percentage given and justified?
If the study evaluates measurement error, is it stated which source of variation (e.g. occasion, rater) was deliberately varied between measurements?

items.topic: ME4 Appropriateness of the time interval
items.question: If the study evaluates measurement error, is the interval between measurements argued to be appropriate?
If the study evaluates measurement error, is it reported whether patients were in fact stable between measurements?
If the study evaluates measurement error, are the statistics reported with their precision, variance components, and systematic differences when limits of agreement are used?

items.topic: CriV1 Justification of the gold standard
items.question: If the study evaluates criterion validity, is it argued that the comparator is a reasonable gold standard?

items.topic: CriV2 Statistics chosen for the criterion
items.question: If the study evaluates criterion validity, are the statistics (correlations, or AUC, sensitivity and specificity for a dichotomous criterion) stated and justified?
If the study evaluates criterion validity, are the results of those statistics reported?

items.section: Construct validity by hypothesis testing: methods
items.question: If the study evaluates construct validity by hypothesis testing, are the expected results stated beforehand, with a rationale for each?

items.section: Construct validity by hypothesis testing: methods
items.question: If the study evaluates construct validity by hypothesis testing, are all statistical methods used to test the hypotheses described?

items.section: Construct validity by hypothesis testing: results
items.question: If the study evaluates construct validity by hypothesis testing, are all results given, each marked as consistent or not with its hypothesis?
If the study evaluates responsiveness, are the hypotheses about change stated, with a rationale for each?

items.topic: Resp2 Intervention or exposure in between
items.question: If the study evaluates responsiveness, is the intervention or exposure between measurements described, or its absence stated?
If the study evaluates responsiveness, are all statistical methods used to test the hypotheses described?
If the study evaluates responsiveness, are the results reported, each marked as consistent or not with its hypothesis?
